title: Redwood Onboarding Kickoff - Larkspur Health
summary: Kickoff for Larkspur Health onboarding to Redwood inference platform. Covered high-level timeline, success criteria, stakeholders, SSO/KMS requirements, VPC/private deployment options, and initial pilot plan on staging. Agreed next steps: share onboarding docs, schedule SE deep dive, and request staging access and SOC2 artifact pack.
action_items: Evan Morales - Send onboarding deck, SSO guide, and security pack - 2027-05-21
Owen Chen - Schedule technical deep dive for integration + initial benchmark plan - 2027-05-24
Samir Patel (customer) - Share CI/CD and firewall/IP allowlist details for staging - 2027-05-22
Priya Shah - Create trial project in Console and invite Larkspur users - 2027-05-21
Tina Alvarez (customer) - Provide SOC2/ISO point of contact and requirements doc - 2027-05-23
next_steps: Redwood to share onboarding materials and SSO/SAML configuration guide
Schedule SE deep dive for model selection and latency targets
Customer to provide allowlist IPs and staging env access
Agree on success criteria for 2-week pilot (latency < 200ms p95 for key flows, cost estimate, data retention policy)
meeting_header: Date: 2027-05-20 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
transcript: [00:00] Evan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:06] Alicia Gomez: Alicia here, Director of Eng at Larkspur — Marcus is our CTO, Tina handles compliance and Samir is our DevOps lead.
[00:15] Marcus Reed: Hi all, thanks. We're trying to move quickly, so appreciate the kickoff.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hi folks, Priya — I'll be your CSM. We'll run the onboarding and make sure timelines are realistic.
[00:27] Owen Chen: Owen, Solutions Eng. I'll lead the deep tech integration and benchmarking.
[00:33] Evan Morales: Agenda — high level timeline, success criteria, SSO/KMS/compliance, decide hosted vs dedicated vs private for pilot, and next steps. Any other items?
[00:40] Tina Alvarez: I'd like to confirm audit logs, retention, and KMS/HSM support — that's a hard requirement for us.
[00:47] Evan Morales: Absolutely, we'll cover that. Quick question on timeline — what's your target for a live pilot?
[00:52] Marcus Reed: Ideally two to three weeks to pilot core flows, then expand. Execs want to see latency and cost numbers by end of June.
[00:59] Priya Shah: That seems doable. For a two-week pilot we usually start with a staging integration and a small subset of traffic.
[01:05] Samir Patel: For staging we need to know IP allowlists and whether we need a VPC peering config or if a private deployment is needed.

[01:11] Owen Chen: For initial pilot we can run on Hosted Redwood with strict data controls, or Dedicated if you want predictable throughput. Private/VPC is available but adds lead time for network setup.
[01:20] Alicia Gomez: What's the typical lead time for Private?

[01:23] Evan Morales: Private deployments generally take 4-6 weeks for full on-prem or VPC setup depending on approvals; dedicated pools are faster — usually a week or two if you have procurement in place.
[01:33] Tina Alvarez: If we do hosted, do you support customer-managed keys? We need KMS integration and audit logs to meet internal policy.

[01:39] Owen Chen: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can surface audit logs via the Console. There was a minor transcription glitch there but yes, HSM/KMS supported and we can ship the SOC2 artifacts.
[01:49] Marcus Reed: Good. Also want to understand routing/fallbacks if capacity issues happen — can requests fallback to a cheaper model?
[01:55] Evan Morales: Smart routing is built in — we can route by latency, cost, or region and set automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants. We'll show that in the SE deep dive.

[02:05] Alicia Gomez: For the success criteria, execs want: functional parity with our current in-house LLM, p95 latency < 200ms for 1k token prompts, and predictable unit cost under $0.015 per prompt. Is that realistic?

[02:16] Owen Chen: Those targets are reasonable for smaller prompts on dedicated instances; we'll need to validate with a benchmark — sequence length, batch sizes will affect numbers. We'll propose a benchmark suite.
[02:26] Priya Shah: We'll work with you on a short prompt set for the pilot and tie quality regressions to that set in Console so you get alerts if outputs degrade.
[02:34] Samir Patel: On integrations, our CI/CD deploys via GitHub Actions; we'll need sample infra as code for the staging connector and an allowlist for Redwood endpoints.
[02:42] Evan Morales: Noted — Owen we'll follow up with the repo examples; Priya will create a trial project and invite the team so you can test Console features.
[02:49] Tina Alvarez: What about data residency? Some PHI concerns might push us to Private for certain workloads.
[02:54] Owen Chen: You can mix modes — sensitive requests can be routed to Private/Dedicated while less sensitive flows hit Hosted. We'll document routing policy configs and data residency controls.
[03:04] Marcus Reed: Good, that's important. Also curious on SSO — SAML or SCIM for provisioning?
[03:09] Evan Morales: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC mapping. We'll send the SSO config guide.
[03:15] Alicia Gomez: Any gotchas around tokens and session length?
[03:18] Owen Chen: Tokens can be short-lived; Console supports session refresh and you can configure token TTLs per policy. We'll share examples.
[03:25] Priya Shah: One note on billing — for pilot we can provide a trial credit and a paced billing estimate; procurement will need an SOW for Dedicated or Private commitments.
[03:33] Marcus Reed: Procurement will want a one-pager with costs and SLAs. Can you include the SLA for Dedicated?
[03:37] Evan Morales: Yes — Dedicated SLA details and uptime/latency targets included in our pricing pack; I'll attach that.
[03:43] Tina Alvarez: Please include security controls: roles, audit logs retention, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS key rot, and compliance contacts.
[03:50] Owen Chen: We'll include the SOC2 report link and a security FAQ; note that some proper nouns in the auto transcript may be off but the artifacts will be correct.
[03:59] Samir Patel: For the staging benchmark, what's a reasonable load to test? We want p95 under 500ms at 50 rps as a start.
[04:05] Owen Chen: 50 rps is high for initial small-scale benchmarking but doable on Dedicated; we'll recommend a phased ramp (5 -> 20 -> 50) and measure p50/p95/p99.

[04:14] Evan Morales: Let's recap: Redwood sends onboarding deck, SSO guide, SOC2 pack, and sample infra repo. Owen schedules deep dive for model selection and benchmarking. Larkspur shares allowlist and staging access. Priya creates Console project and invites users.
[04:26] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side for next week? Marcus?
[04:30] Marcus Reed: We'll get the allowlist and security POC contact to Tina by Friday. Procurement might take longer but pilot shouldn't require full procurement.
[04:37] Priya Shah: I'll send calendar invites for the technical deep dive; Owen will lead. Evan will send the security & pricing artifacts after this call.
[04:44] Tina Alvarez: One last question — can you confirm retention windows for logs and ability to configure retention?
[04:49] Owen Chen: Yes you can configure retention per project and we support export of logs to your SIEM. We'll include steps in the security doc.
[04:56] Evan Morales: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up within 24 hours with docs and next steps. Meeting adjourned.
[04:59] (end of recording)
